sentences.text: JUDGMENT

Wife and daughters of deceased Rangaiah filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 alleging that on 02.07.2024 at 15.30 hours, when Rangaiah was walking/standing on the left side of Kadehalli village circle, Dabbeghatta hobli, Turuvekere taluk, driver of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44- 9670 drove the same negligently from Melinavalagerehalli side turned towards Dabbeghatta , dashed the same to Rangaiah, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Rangaiah.

2. Immediately after the accident Rangaiah has been shifted to Adichunchanagiri hospital,
B.G.Nagara, Nagamangala, wherein on 05.07.2024 Rangaiah succumbed to the injuries.

3. As on the date of accident deceased Rangaiah being aged 64 years , used to earn Rs.25,000/p.m.
by doing agriculture and vending milk, used to contribute the entire income to the family.
4.
Regarding accident Turuvekere police registered a case in Crime No.128/2024 against the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 .
5. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 owner of the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 remained absent.

6. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident , age,

2 occupation and income of the deceased Rangaiah.

7. On the basis of the pleadings on 28.01.2025, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 02.07.2024 at about 15.30 hours, beside road at Kadehalli village circle, Dabbeghatta Hobli, Turuvekere Taluk, Tumkur district, in view of the negligent use of the lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-44-9617, lorry dashed to Rangaiah , S/o. Kempaiah, thereby accident taken place resulting in the grievous injuries to Rangaiah who succumbed to those injuries on 05.07.2024 a Adichunchanagiri hospital , Bellur?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation ?

If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
8. On 06.03.2025, petitioner No.1/Rangamma deposed as RW1, produced 19 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.19.
On 29.03.2025 learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner produced copy of the permit pertaining to Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 at Ex.P.20.
9. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

10. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.9,41,434/- with current and future interest at 6%p..a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-

Turuvekere taluk, driver of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 drove the same negligently from Melinavalagerehalli side turned towards Dabbeghatta , dashed the same to her husband Rangaiah,
thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Rangaiah.
12.

PW1 further stated that immediately after the accident, her husband Rangaiah has been admitted to Adichunchanagiri hospital, B.G.Nagara, Nagamangala, wherein on 05.07.2024 Rangaiah succumbed to the injuries.
13. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident .
14. In the cross-examination, PW1 submitted she never witnessed the accident.

sentences.text: Ex .P.1 is the copy of the FIR with complaint pertaining to crime No.128/24 registered by Turuvekere police on 03.07.2024 at 16.00 hours against the driver of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 for having committed offence punishable under Section 281, 125(a) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) on the basis of the complaint presented by Jayaram, S/o.Bhojaiah.
16. Ex.P.2 is the copy of information forwarded by PSI, Turuvekere police station on 05.07.2024 to Senior Civil Judge and JMFC , Turuvekere about the death of Rangaiah.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar and sketch of place of accident , Ex.P.4 is vehicle seizure mahazar with photos.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of the inquest mahazar , Ex.P.6 is the copy of P.M.Report.
Ex.P.8 is the Motor Vehicle Accident report.

Ex.P.9 is the copy of chargesheet filed by Turuvekere police in Crime No.128/2024 against Dhanaraju, S/o.Giriyappa, driver of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 for having committed offence punishable under Section 281, 106 of the Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) .

17. The medical bills and records shows that since from the time of accident till 05.07.2024,
petitioners get treated Rangaiah at Adichunchanagiri hospital , Nagamangala however, during treatment on 05.07.2024 Ragaiah expired.
18. In this case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

19. Hence, I have concluded that on 02.07.2024 at 15.30 hours, when Rangaiah was standing on the left side of Kadehalli village circle, Dhanaraj, S/o. Giriyappa negligently drove Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 from Melinavalagerehalli turned towards Dabbeghatta dashed the same to Rangaiah, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Rangaiah, who succumbed to those injuries at Adichunchanagiri hospital , Nagamangala on 05.07.2024.
Hence, I answer issue No. 1 in the Affirmative .

20. Issue No.2: In the evidence PW1 stated that as on the date of accident her husband deceased Rangaiah being aged 64 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/p.m. by doing agriculture and vending milk,
used to contribute entire income to the family.
21. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of the deceased.
22. In the cross-examination, PW1 admitted that as per MLC Register extract on the date of accident her husband was aged about 70 years.
PW1 admitted lack of documents to show that as on the date of accident her husband used to earn Rs.25,000/p.m.
In the P.M.Report and inquest mahazar age of the deceased is noted as 65 years.
In the aadhar card marked at Ex.P.10 date of birth of deceased Rangaiah is noted as 01.01.1957.
In the medical records age of the deceased is noted as 67 to 70 years.
In the file there are no documents regarding occupation, income of deceased.
23. The copy of aadhar cards shows that petitioners are the wife and daughters of deceased Rangaiah.

Hence, I have inferred that it is fit and proper to calculate compensation under the head of loss of dependency presuming that as on the date of incident deceased Rangaiah being aged 67 to Rangamma vs Chandrashekhar on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167664152/
4 70 years, monthly notional income as on the date of accident is Rs.16,500/-, deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses and by applying multiplier 5 in the following terms:
Age of the deceased Rangaiah as on the 67-70 years date of accident - Monthly notional income of deceased - Rs.16,500/- Rangaiah as on the date of accident Less : 1/ 3rd towards personal expenses of Rs.11,000/- the deceased Rangaiah (16,500 - 5,500/- = 11,000) Annual income of the deceased 11,000x12 Rs.1,32,000/- Loss of dependency 1,32,000x5 Rs.6,60,000/-
24.
Hence, I award Rs.6,60,000/- towards loss of dependency.

Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses , Rs.44,000/- towards spousal consortium to petitioner No.1,
Rs.1,32,000/- towards parental consortium to petitioners No.2 to 4 at the rate of Rs.44,000/- each.

25. The medical bills shows that since from the time of accident till 05.07.2024 petitioners get treated Rangaiah by spending Rs.67,434/- towards treatment charges, Rs.5,000/- towards attendant, conveyance charges.

26. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners being wife and daughters of deceased Rangaiah are entitle to receive Rs.9,41,434/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
as compensation from the respondents.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly.
27. Issue No.3:
In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company admitted that as on the date of accident Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
Copy of the permit marked at Ex.P.20 shows that as on the date of incident Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 had permit to run in Karnataka.
In the reply submitted to Investigation Officer to the notice issued under Section 133 of IMV Act, the respondent No.1 noted D.L. Number of Dhanaraj, S/o. Giriyappa.
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of accident respondent No.1 has not violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that respondents being the Rangamma vs Chandrashekhar on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167664152/
5 owner and insurer of the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44- 9670 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners.

sentences.text:
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.9,41,434/- (Rupees nine lakhs forty one thousand four hundred and thirty four only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Tipper lorry bearing No.KA-44-9670 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners at the ratio of 70:10:10:10.

After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioners No.1 to 4 may be released by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 8th day of April , 2025) (J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T. Bengaluru.
